title: fix(devx): retire the dead CI half of the lockfile merge driver, move the anti-vacuity weight
body:
Fixes #6436

Implements the maintainer ruling of 2026-08-27 (「同意，并继续」, option B): remove the measured-dead CI half of the `pnpm-lock.yaml` merge driver, keep the measured-live contributor half, and re-point the guide at what the mechanism now is — contributor-facing, with zero CI consumers.

All verification below ran against `981423c47`, the head of this branch.

## Constraint 1 — which assertion now carries the anti-vacuity weight

⭐ **This is the load-bearing part of the change.** The retired `configuring.length > 0` guard was doing **two** jobs, and each has a new, named owner. Nothing was flipped to `=== 0`; the count assertion is gone entirely.

| The retired guard proved… | …is now proved by |
|:--|:--|
| the grep matched something, so a zero is a reading rather than a scan that read nothing | **`it('the workflow scan is live — zero configuring workflows is a reading, not a broken grep')`** — a control term that MUST hit the same population (`git config`, which `changelog.yml` genuinely runs), read out of the same directory by the same reader |
| the mechanism still had a consumer at all | **`it('keeps the .gitattributes half of the mechanism true')`** and **`it("keeps CONTRIBUTING.md's contributor path — the mechanism's only remaining consumer")`** — those two files *are* the mechanism now |

The **phantom direction** is load-bearing on its own for the first time: with zero configuring workflows, `phantom` is exactly "workflows this page still names", so a resurrected row reddens by itself instead of riding along with a count that happened to be non-zero. The `missing` direction becomes the tripwire for a CI consumer returning.

⭐ The second row is where the real weight landed. The old guard asked *"does anything still consume this driver?"* and answered with a workflow count. That count is zero by ruling, so the question is answered at the consumer that was measured live — and the failure message is the old one re-pointed: if CONTRIBUTING.md stops defining the driver, the mechanism genuinely has no consumers and the section plus the `.gitattributes` line should be deleted with it.

### Proved by ablation, not asserted

Committed first, so each restore leg had the implementation to return to. Every mutation was confirmed on disk by counting both the removed and the injected token (an editor's exit code proves nothing), and every restore was proved byte-for-byte against the `HEAD` blob hash.

| # | Ablation | Result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| A1 | delete the `.gitattributes` line | `keeps the .gitattributes half` **RED** |
| A2 | delete CONTRIBUTING.md's driver definition | `only remaining consumer` **RED** |
| A3 | put a workflow row back in the guide table | both-directions **RED** (phantom) |
| A4 | break the scan's control term | `the workflow scan is live` **RED** |
| A4b | the both-directions pin under that *same* broken scan | **GREEN** |
| A5 | a workflow configures the driver again | both-directions **RED** (missing) |

⭐ **A4b is the point of the whole exercise.** Under a broken scan the both-directions pin still passes — that is precisely the vacuity the retired guard existed to catch, and the new control test is what now catches it. Restore proof: `git diff HEAD` empty over all five targets, and all five worktree hashes equal to their `HEAD` blobs.

## Constraint 2 — the worked-example citation, re-pointed a second time

`scripts/check-pre-install-import-graph.mjs` and its test cited `changeset-release.yml`'s config as *the* worked example of "a quoted argument that must not be read as an install". This PR removes that config, so the citation is re-pointed for the second time (PR #6389 was the first, from `dependabot-auto-merge.yml`) — and this time no live in-repo example remains.

Honest "formerly" wording, ⛔ not a silent deletion: the anchor now says the example was formerly `changeset-release.yml`, that no live instance is left, and that the shape survives as the synthetic fixture in the test — **cited by the test case's name, not by a line number**. That last choice is #6998's own recommendation, applied to the text this PR writes; #6998 records a cross-file citation in this repo that had rotted 86 and 107 lines off. (The dispatch's own `:273-278` had already drifted to 275-276, so the citation was located by content.)

A **third** copy of the same citation turned up during the sweep — `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md` also cited that config as the gate's worked example. My diff falsifies it, so it is re-pointed the same way rather than left behind.

## Constraint 3

#6437 is untouched and stays open. Nothing here closes it: this PR fixes the *model* for the case the ruling decided, and the CI-only framing #6437 describes is a separate subject. The commit trailer says `Part of #6436` while this body carries the `Fixes`, so the squashed message cannot contradict itself.

## Prose my diff falsified, and fixed

Removing the config makes three statements elsewhere untrue. All three are corrected rather than left to rot:

- `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md`, changeset-release section: *"Both lanes configure a pnpm-lock.yaml merge driver"* → they configure none, with the reason.
- The same page's pre-install-import-graph prose (the third citation copy above).
- `.github/workflows/changeset-release.yml:557`'s comment already argued the `.gitattributes` half "is NOT dead" — correct, and on the ruling's side, but it explained a config that is no longer beside it. It is now a tombstone that keeps the whole measurement record (the enumerated `git` sweep, each zero-hit with its control term, and the `changesets/action@v1.9.0` reading) so nobody re-derives it a fourth time.

⚠️ One trap worth naming: the pin greps workflow text for the config key, so merely **naming** that key in a workflow comment trips it. That is the safe direction — a false red, never a false green — and the tombstone comment spells the attribute form instead. Both the comment and the pin's failure message say so.

## Verification

Everything below ran on `981423c47`.

- `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 scripts/__tests__` → **90 files, 2574 tests, all passed**, exit 0.
- Gates, each exit code captured before any pipe: `check:control-bytes`, `check:doc-fences`, `check:doc-types`, `check:pre-install-import-graph`, `check:action-forward-parity`, `check:shell-escape-residue`, `docs:check-links` → all **exit 0**.
- `check:doc-snippets` first returned **exit 2** — "I could not run", not a red. Built the closure it names (`turbo run build $(node scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs --build-filter) --concurrency=2`, 32/32 tasks) and re-ran: **271 of 271 blocks judged, 0 failed**, exit 0.
- `check-changeset-presence` with `GITHUB_BASE_REF=main` → exit 0. The changeset carries **empty frontmatter**: repository tooling and contributor docs, publishing nothing. ⛔ No `skip-changeset` label — in this repo that label is a phantom with zero readers.
- `pnpm lint:root` → exit 0. Not narrowed: the full scoped population ran — **221 files judged** (counted from eslint's own `--format json`, not estimated), 0 errors, 29 pre-existing warnings, none in this diff. All three lintable files this PR edits were in that population at 0 errors / 0 warnings.
- Control-byte self-scan across every file in the diff, beyond the gate: clean.

The test surface was derived from what the diff touches rather than from the dispatch list: `git grep` for every file that references `ci-cd-pipeline.md`, `.gitattributes`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `changeset-release.yml` returned 20 files, all inside `scripts/` — so the tree run above covers them, and the doc/lint gates cover the rest.
